skill.name: aippt
skill.description: Generate presentation images from an existing PowerPoint template, then package the images into a PPTX file.
skill.summary: A template-guided workflow for planning slides, generating styled images, and packaging a presentation.
skill.author: Ceeon

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed that the documented workflow uploads local images to third-party image hosts and calls an external image-generation API. Most static alerts are Markdown delimiters, package-lock metadata, or entropy heuristics and are false positives. No prompt-injection language or hidden executable payload was found in the reviewed documentation.

remediation.issue: The recommended image-hosting command embeds a reusable third-party API key in documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the key, require users to supply their own key through a protected local configuration method, and revoke or rotate the exposed key.

remediation.issue: The workflow recommends uploading presentation images to public third-party hosts.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the privacy implications, require explicit user confirmation before upload, and offer a private or self-hosted storage option.

remediation.issue: The external image API example sends prompts and a bearer token through curl.
remediation.suggestion: Document the destination, data handling, cost, and credential-storage requirements before users run the request.

content.value_statement: Creating a consistent presentation from a template requires repeated layout and image work. This skill guides template analysis, slide planning, image generation, and PPTX packaging.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to export PowerPoint slides as reference images on macOS and Windows.
Guides analysis of a presentation template to identify reusable layouts.
Helps divide source content into a page-by-page presentation plan.
Maps planned content to template layouts and image-generation prompts.
Documents image upload and external generation steps for reference images.
Packages ordered image files into a 16:9 PPTX with the included Node.js workflow.
limitations: It requires an existing PowerPoint template and local tools for export and packaging.
Image generation quality and availability depend on external services and user credentials.
Uploading reference images can expose confidential presentation material to third parties.
The skill does not guarantee editable PowerPoint elements because it packages slide images.

use_cases.title: Refresh a branded sales deck
use_cases.description: Turn approved sales content into slides that follow an existing company template.

use_cases.title: Prepare a course presentation
use_cases.description: Plan lesson content by page and create visual slides with a consistent course style.

use_cases.title: Build a client proposal
use_cases.description: Use a proposal template to organize sections and produce a draft slide deck efficiently.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a simple deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my template and this outline to propose a six-slide presentation plan. List the purpose and key message for each slide.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a template
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this PowerPoint template. Identify its recurring layouts, title areas, image areas, and text hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Map content to layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this presentation plan to the template layout library. For each slide, explain the selected layout and draft an image-generation prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare production steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production checklist for this deck. Include reference-image export, privacy review before upload, image generation, download validation, and PPTX packaging.

output_examples.input: Create a five-slide project update from this outline and template.
output: Slide 1: Project status and reporting period
Slide 2: Completed milestones with supporting visuals

output_examples.input: Analyze the template layout for a comparison slide.
output: Recommended layout: two equal content columns
Use: compare options, benefits, or timelines
Prompt guidance: preserve the template colors, spacing, and typography

best_practices: Review all images and prompts for confidential information before using an external service.
Use a licensed template and verify that generated images match the intended brand style.
Inspect the final PPTX for slide order, aspect ratio, readability, and image quality.
anti_patterns: Do not upload confidential images to a public image host without explicit approval.
Do not place real API keys directly in prompts, scripts, or documentation.
Do not assume packaged image slides remain editable as native PowerPoint objects.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It guides creation of slide images and packaging them into a PPTX presentation.

faq.question: Do I need an existing template?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses a PowerPoint template as the visual reference.

faq.question: Can I use my own image service?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a service approved for your data and adapt the upload and generation steps.

faq.question: Are the slides editable?
faq.answer: The packaged slides are images, so individual text and shapes are not native editable elements.

faq.question: How should I store API keys?
faq.answer: Keep keys in protected local configuration and never commit them to source control.

faq.question: What should I check before delivery?
faq.answer: Check confidentiality, image quality, slide order, aspect ratio, and presentation readability.
